pattern.title: respectful action
pattern.explain: Put -(으)시- inside a word to show respect for the person doing the action, like a teacher or elder: 들어오셨어요 = (they) came in.
pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -시- after a vowel (가시다), -으시- after a consonant (읽으시다). It comes before tense markers and endings (가셨어요, 가시겠어요).

examples.en: The teacher came into the classroom.
My father reads the newspaper.

pattern.note: Use it only for the subject being honored, never for yourself; do not add it to 있다 (use 계시다) or to 먹다 (use 드시다).

practice.scene: A traveler on the KTX from Seoul to Busan finds someone sitting in seat 7C, which is on her ticket. The other passenger checks his ticket and realizes he is in the wrong car, and she kindly helps him find the right one.

pattern.title: formal polite statement
pattern.explain: Put -ㅂ니다/습니다 at the end of an action or description to speak in a formal, respectful way: 갑니다 = I go.
pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -ㅂ니다 after a vowel (갑니다), -습니다 after a consonant (먹습니다). Stems ending in ㄹ drop the ㄹ (살다 → 삽니다).

pattern.title: everyday polite ending
pattern.explain: Put -아요/어요 at the end of an action or description for friendly, polite daily speech: 마셔요 = I drink.
pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -아요 if the last vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ (좋아요), otherwise -어요 (먹어요). 하다 becomes 해요, and many stems contract (가다 → 가요, 마시다 → 마셔요).

examples.en: I drink coffee every day.
The weather is really nice.

pattern.note: The same form works as a statement, question, suggestion or command; intonation and context tell them apart.

practice.scene: A patient arrives at a clinic for a 3 p.m. appointment for a sore throat and wants to check in, but the receptionist says the insurance card needs to be shown and the form filled out first.

pattern.title: plain written style

paragraph: 교수님, 늦어서 죄송합니다. 무슨 일입니까? 지하철이 왜 멈췄는지 모르겠지만 십 분이나 지연되었습니다. 자리에 앉아도 되는지 여쭤봐도 되겠습니까? 네, 앉으십시오. 놓친 부분이 무엇인지 친구에게 물어보십시오.
translation: Professor, I'm sorry I'm late. What happened? I don't know why the subway stopped, but it was delayed by ten whole minutes. May I ask whether I may take my seat? Yes, please sit. Ask a friend what part you missed.

pattern.title: whether, how, what
pattern.explain: Use -는지 inside a sentence to ask or say where, how, or whether: 어디에 사는지 = where (someone) lives.
pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -는지 (가는지, 먹는지); adjective stem + -(으)ㄴ지 (예쁜지, 작은지); noun + -인지. For the past use -았/었는지.

examples.en: Do you know where that person lives?
I don't know what the weather will be like tomorrow.

pattern.note: It is used inside a sentence with verbs like 알다, 모르다, 묻다; in these questions use a question word or 'whether'.

practice.scene: A university student arrives ten minutes late to a morning lecture because the subway was delayed. She quietly apologizes to the professor at the door and asks whether she may take her seat.

paragraph: 할아버지, 새해 복 많이 받으십시오. 항상 건강하십시오. 그래, 고맙다. 올해는 학교에서 무엇을 하고 싶은지 말해 보아라. 영어를 열심히 공부하고 싶습니다. 그런데 어떤 학원이 좋은지 아직 모르겠습니다. 천천히 알아보아라. 자, 세뱃돈이다. 맛있는 것도 사 먹어라.
translation: Grandfather, happy New Year. Please always stay healthy. Yes, thank you. Tell me what you want to do at school this year. I want to study English hard. But I don't know yet which academy is good. Take your time finding out. Here, your New Year's money. Buy something tasty to eat too.

paragraph: 약사님, 이 약 세 알은 하루에 몇 번 먹어야 해요? 하루에 세 번, 식사 후에 드세요. 커피도 마셔도 돼요? 저는 하루에 세 잔씩 마셨었거든요. 당분간은 피하세요. 저도 예전에 위가 안 좋았었는데, 커피를 끊고 나아졌어요. 아, 그렇군요. 그럼 커피 대신 물을 많이 마실게요.
translation: Pharmacist, how many times a day should I take these three pills? Take them three times a day, after meals. Is it okay to drink coffee too? I used to drink three cups a day. Avoid it for a while. I used to have a bad stomach too, and I got better after quitting coffee. Oh, I see. Then I'll drink lots of water instead of coffee.

pattern.meaning: did in the past (no longer true)
pattern.title: used to, but no more
pattern.explain: Use -았/었었- for something that was true in the past but isn't anymore: 살았었어요 = I used to live there.
pattern.attaches: Past stem + -았었- if the last vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ, otherwise -었었- (갔었어요, 먹었었어요). 하다 becomes 했었-.

examples.en: I used to live in Busan when I was young.
This cafe used to be quiet.

pattern.note: It implies the situation is no longer true or is cut off from the present. Do not use it for something that still continues.

practice.scene: After a visit, a patient asks the pharmacist how often to take the three pills and whether it is okay to drink coffee. The pharmacist explains to take them after meals, three times a day, and to avoid coffee.

paragraph: 어, 구름이 엄청 까맣네. 너 일기예보 봤어? 응, 봤어. 점심 먹고 나서 비 온대. 그래? 아침엔 맑았었는데. 우산 챙겨야겠다. 지난주에도 우산 안 가져가서 다 젖었었잖아. 맞다, 그때 진짜 심했었지. 오늘은 꼭 들고 가자.
translation: Oh, the clouds are really dark. Did you check the forecast? Yeah, I did. They say it'll rain after lunch. Really? It was clear this morning. I'd better bring an umbrella. Last week too we didn't take umbrellas and got soaked, remember? Right, that was really bad. Let's be sure to carry one today.

paragraph: 팀장님, 안녕하십니까. 김민지입니다. 지하철 2호선이 신호 문제로 멈췄습니다. 아, 그렇습니까? 언제쯤 도착할 수 있습니까? 9시 출근 시간보다 30분쯤 늦을 것 같습니다. 이전에도 한 번 멈췄었는데, 그때는 금방 복구됐었습니다. 알겠습니다. 그럼 9시 30분 회의에는 전화로 참석할 수 있습니까? 네, 전화로 참석하겠습니다.
translation: Team leader, good morning. This is Minji Kim. Subway line 2 has stopped because of a signal problem. Oh, is that so? About when can you arrive? I think I'll be about 30 minutes later than the 9:00 start. It stopped once before too, but that time it was restored quickly. Understood. Then can you join the 9:30 meeting by phone? Yes, I will join by phone.

paragraph: 김 대리, 좋은 아침입니다. 어젯밤에 잘 잤습니까? 안녕하십니까, 이사님. 네, 잘 잤습니다. 예전에는 낯선 곳에서 잠을 잘 못 잤었는데 어제는 푹 잤습니다. 다행입니다. 저도 젊을 때는 이 호수를 자주 걸었었습니다. 8시 아침 식사 전에 같이 걷겠습니까? 네, 좋습니다. 같이 걷겠습니다.

paragraph: 안녕하십니까? 지난주에 온라인으로 산 청바지를 교환하고 싶습니다. 주문한 바와 달리 30 사이즈가 왔습니다. 불편을 드려 죄송합니다. 확인해 본 바로는 28 사이즈로 주문하셨네요. 영수증을 보여 주시겠습니까? 여기 있습니다. 제가 알고 있는 바로는 일주일 안에는 환불도 가능하다고 들었습니다. 네, 저희 규정에 정해진 바에 따라 교환이나 환불 중 원하시는 것으로 처리해 드리겠습니다. 그럼 28 사이즈로 교환해 주십시오.
translation: Hello. I'd like to exchange the jeans I bought online last week. Contrary to what I ordered, a size 30 arrived. I apologize for the inconvenience. As far as I've checked, you ordered a size 28. May I see your receipt? Here it is. As far as I know, I heard a refund is also possible within a week. Yes, in accordance with what our policy stipulates, we will process whichever you prefer, exchange or refund. Then please exchange it for a size 28.

pattern.title: as far as, the way
pattern.explain: A formal way to say what or how, often with knowing: 제가 아는 바로는 = as far as I know.
pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -는 바 (present), -(으)ㄴ 바 (past), -(으)ㄹ 바 (future); adjectives take -(으)ㄴ 바. 바 is a bound noun, so it is followed by a particle such as 로, 에 or 를.

pattern.note: It is formal and used in writing and speeches; don't use it for casual conversation.

practice.scene: A customer returns a pair of jeans bought online last week because the delivered size was 30 instead of 28. The staff member at the service desk asks for the receipt and offers an exchange or a refund.

paragraph: 안내해 드린 바와 같이 검사 전날 밤 9시 이후에는 금식하셔야 합니다. 물도 마시면 안 됩니까? 제가 들은 바로는 물은 괜찮다고 하던데요. 병원 지침에 나와 있는 바에 따르면 소량의 물은 가능합니다. 다만 커피는 안 됩니다. 알겠습니다. 결과는 언제 알 수 있습니까? 제가 알고 있는 바로는 일주일 뒤에 우편으로 도착합니다.
translation: As I have explained, you must fast after 9 p.m. the night before the checkup. Is water not allowed either? As far as I heard, water was fine. According to what the hospital guidelines say, a small amount of water is possible. But coffee is not. Understood. When can I find out the results? As far as I know, they arrive by mail in a week.

paragraph: 강아지가 정말 귀엽네요! 이름이 뭐예요? 콩이예요. 이제 네 달 됐어요. 아직 아기네요. 산책할 때 다른 강아지를 보면 어때요? 겁이 많아서 다른 강아지를 보면 제 뒤에 숨곤 해요. 우리 강아지도 어릴 때 그러곤 했어요. 금방 괜찮아질 거예요.
translation: The puppy is so cute! What's its name? It's Kong. It's four months old now. It's still a baby. How is it when it sees other dogs on walks? It's timid, so it often hides behind me when it sees other dogs. Our dog used to do that too when it was little. It'll be fine soon.

pattern.title: used to, often do
pattern.explain: Add -곤 하다 after an action to say you did it again and again in the past: 가곤 했어요 = used to go.
pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -곤 하다, the same after a vowel or a consonant (가곤 하다, 먹곤 하다). It is a contraction of -고는 하다.

examples.en: This is the teacher's book.
I am going to my friend's house.

pattern.note: 의 is pronounced [에] when it is the possessive marker, and it is often dropped, as in 제 친구 or 우리 집.

pattern.title: or
pattern.explain: Add N(이)나 between choices to say 'or': 영화나 드라마 = a movie or a drama.
pattern.attaches: Noun + 이나 after a consonant (빵이나), 나 after a vowel (커피나). For 'or', it joins two nouns (빵이나 밥); for 'as many as', it follows an amount.

examples.en: On weekends I watch a movie or a drama.

pattern.note: After an amount, it means more than expected; do not use it for neutral quantities.

pattern.title: until, up to

pattern.attaches: Attaches directly to a noun, after a vowel or a consonant (오늘까지, 서울까지). It marks an endpoint of time or place, or 'even' for an extreme example.

examples.en: I work until six in the afternoon.

pattern.title: until, up to

pattern.attaches: Attaches directly to a noun, after a vowel or a consonant (오늘까지, 서울까지). It marks an endpoint of time or place, or 'even' for an extreme example.

pattern.title: only

pattern.title: from a person

examples.en: I received a present from my friend.
I heard this story from my mother.

pattern.note: It is used only for people or animals; for places use N에서. In speech, 한테 alone often replaces 한테서 with verbs like 받다 and 듣다.

pattern.title: about, around

pattern.attaches: Attaches directly to a noun of time, number, or amount, after a vowel or a consonant (세 시쯤, 열 명쯤). It is used for rough estimates.

pattern.title: only (nothing but)

pattern.attaches: Attaches directly to a noun (usually an amount), after a vowel or a consonant (하나밖에, 천 원밖에). It must be followed by a negative predicate.

examples.en: I have only 1,000 won now.

pattern.title: about, regarding

pattern.title: for the sake of

pattern.attaches: Noun + 을 after a consonant (가족을 위해), 를 after a vowel (친구를 위해), then 위해(서).

examples.en: Anyone can enter this room.

examples.en: Tell me anything.

pattern.note: Usually used with question words (누구, 뭐, 언제, 어디) to mean any-; 든지 is often shortened to 든.

paragraph: 안녕하세요! 목요일 저녁 6시 반에 고깃집에서 같이 식사할래요? 그날 6시까지 치과 예약이 있어요. 치료에 따라 더 걸릴 수도 있어서요. 그럼 7시 반으로 미룰까요? 저는 괜찮아요. 좋아요. 그날 상황에 따라 조금 늦을 수도 있는데 괜찮아요? 그럼요. 제가 7시 반으로 예약할게요.

I'll book it for 7:30.

pattern.attaches: Attaches directly to a noun, with no change after a vowel or a consonant (이름조차).

examples.en: I was so busy I couldn't even eat a meal.
That person doesn't even know my name.

pattern.note: 조차 is normally used with a negative predicate and suggests that something expected is lacking.

practice.scene: An HR officer at a company calls a job applicant to confirm the interview time on Wednesday at 10 a.m. and explains what documents to bring. The applicant confirms and asks where to go in the building.

paragraph: 실례합니다. 산책 코스는 어디에서 시작합니까? 안내소 옆 입구에서 시작합니다. 한 바퀴 도는 데 약 40분 걸립니다. 처음 와서 길조차 잘 모르는데 지도가 있습니까? 네, 여기 있습니다. 마지막 입장은 오후 5시이고, 5시가 지나면 입구조차 들어가실 수 없습니다. 알겠습니다. 바로 출발하겠습니다. 감사합니다.
translation: Excuse me. Where does the walking route start? It starts at the entrance next to the information desk. It takes about 40 minutes to go around once. It's my first visit and I don't even know the way well. Do you have a map? Yes, here you are. The last entry is at 5 p.m., and after 5 you can't even get through the entrance. Understood. I'll set off right away. Thank you.

pattern.title: for a, considering
pattern.explain: Add N치고 after a word to say how someone is surprising for that group: 학생치고 = for a student.
pattern.attaches: Attaches directly to a noun, with no change after a vowel or a consonant (학생치고).

You speak Korean well for a foreigner.

pattern.note: 치고 often introduces a general rule about a class, with the second clause stating something against or in line with expectation.

paragraph: 안녕하십니까, 지원자님. 인사팀입니다. 수요일 오전 10시 면접 일정을 확인드리려고 연락드렸습니다. 네, 안녕하십니까. 수요일 오전 10시에 찾아뵙겠습니다. 이력서와 신분증, 졸업증명서를 가져오십시오. 경력직치고 서류가 적은 편입니다. 알겠습니다. 그런데 어디로 가면 됩니까? 본관 3층 인사팀으로 오십시오. 대기업치고 건물이 작아서 찾기 쉬우실 겁니다. 감사합니다. 수요일에 뵙겠습니다.

pattern.title: shall we…?
pattern.explain: Use -(으)ㄹ까요? to suggest doing something together or offer to do something: 볼까요? = shall we watch?
pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -을까요? after a consonant (먹을까요?), -ㄹ까요? after a vowel (갈까요?); ㄹ-stem verbs drop ㄹ before ㄹ (만들까요?).

examples.en: Shall we watch a movie together this weekend?
Shall I open the door?

pattern.note: With 우리 or an implied 'we' it is a suggestion; with 제가 it offers to do something.

practice.scene: A guest asks the front desk until what time breakfast is served and where the restaurant is. The clerk explains it is on the 2nd floor until 10 a.m., but weekends end at 10:30.

pattern.title: please do / polite
pattern.explain: Add -(으)세요 to an action word to politely ask someone to do something or to say what an older person does: 읽으세요 = please read.
pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -세요 after a vowel (가세요), -으세요 after a consonant (읽으세요). Stems ending in ㄹ drop the ㄹ (살다 → 사세요).

examples.en: My mother is reading a book now.
Please sit here.

pattern.note: Some verbs use special honorific forms, such as 드세요 (먹다/마시다), 주무세요 (자다) and 계세요 (있다).

practice.scene: An employee calls her team leader in the morning to say she has a fever and can't come in today. The team leader tells her to rest and asks her to send a file if she can.

pattern.title: let's
pattern.explain: Use -자 with friends or people younger than you to suggest doing something together: 먹자 = let's eat.
pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -자, with no change for vowels or consonants (가자, 먹자); used with action verbs only.

examples.en: Let's eat dinner together tonight.
The weather is nice, so let's go to the park.

pattern.note: This is informal 반말 for close friends or juniors, so avoid it with elders; the polite form is -아요/어요 or -(으)ㅂ시다.

practice.scene: Two close friends text about Saturday. Minji wants to go hiking at Bukhansan, but Joon says rain is forecast and suggests a movie in Gangnam instead.

paragraph: 약사님, 이 약은 하루에 몇 번 먹어요? 알약 세 개를 식후에 하루 세 번 드세요. 밥을 먹고 바로 먹는 게 어때요? 아침에 밥을 안 먹으면 어떡해요? 커피만 마시는 게 어때요? 커피는 위에 안 좋아요. 빵이라도 조금 먹는 게 어때요? 아, 그렇군요. 그럼 커피는 약 먹는 동안 피할게요.

paragraph: 미국에 있는 언니한테 겨울옷 3킬로그램을 보내고 싶은데요, EMS는 얼마나 걸려요? EMS는 3일에서 5일쯤 걸리고, 일반 항공 우편은 2주쯤 걸려요. 급하면 EMS로 보내지 그래요? 요금은 얼마나 차이가 나요? EMS는 6만 원이고 일반은 2만 5천 원이에요. 겨울옷이니까 싼 걸로 보내지 그래요? 그럼 일반으로 보낼게요. 조금 늦어도 괜찮아요.
translation: I want to send 3 kilograms of winter clothes to my sister in the US. How long does EMS take? EMS takes about 3 to 5 days, and regular airmail takes about 2 weeks. If it's urgent, why don't you send it by EMS? How big is the difference in price? EMS is 60,000 won and regular is 25,000 won. Since they're winter clothes, why don't you send them the cheaper way? Then I'll send it by regular mail. It's fine if it's a little late.

paragraph: 일요일에 할머니 댁에 같이 가자. 할머니가 너 보고 싶대. 어떡하지? 일요일 아침에 친구들이랑 축구하기로 했어. 축구는 몇 시에 끝나? 끝나고 오후에 가지 그래? 두 시쯤 끝나. 그런데 많이 지칠 것 같아. 그럼 씻고 좀 쉬었다가 저녁에 가지 그래? 할머니가 저녁 해 주신대. 좋아, 그럼 여섯 시까지 갈게.
translation: Let's go to Grandma's house together on Sunday. She says she wants to see you. What should I do? I promised to play soccer with my friends on Sunday morning. What time does soccer end? Why don't you go in the afternoon after it ends? It ends around two. But I think I'll be really tired. Then why don't you wash up, rest a bit, and go in the evening? Grandma says she'll make dinner. Okay, then I'll get there by six.

pattern.title: soft question

pattern.title: to go and do

pattern.attaches: Adjective or verb stem + -게, with no change for final consonants. It turns an adjective into an adverb or expresses purpose or result.

paragraph: 미국에 있는 언니한테 겨울옷을 보내려고요. EMS는 얼마나 걸려요? EMS는 3일쯤 걸리고 6만 원이에요. 일반 항공우편은 2주쯤 걸리고 3만 원이에요. 언니가 급하지 않아서 천천히 받기로 했어요. 항공우편으로 할게요. 네, 그럼 항공우편으로 보내기로 하신 거죠? 여기에 주소를 써 주세요.
translation: I'm sending winter clothes to my sister in the US. How long does EMS take? EMS takes about 3 days and costs 60,000 won. Regular airmail takes about 2 weeks and costs 30,000 won. My sister isn't in a hurry, so we agreed she'd receive it slowly. I'll go with airmail. Yes, so you've decided to send it by airmail, right? Please write the address here.

pattern.title: decide to
pattern.explain: Use -기로 하다 to say you decided or agreed to do something: 만나기로 했어요 = we decided to meet.
pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -기로 하다 after both vowels and consonants (가기로 하다, 먹기로 하다).

examples.en: I decided to meet my friend tomorrow.

pattern.note: It expresses a decision or agreement already made, so it is usually in the past tense (-기로 했어요).

paragraph: 저, 적금 통장을 만들고 싶어요. 여권을 가져왔어요. 외국인 등록증도 있어야 해요. 여권만으로는 안 돼요. 아, 오늘은 안 가져왔어요. 다른 은행에서 물어 보니까 여권만 되던데요. 저희가 확인해 보니까 적금은 등록증이 꼭 필요해요. 내일 다시 오시겠어요? 네, 집에 가서 찾아 보니 서랍에 있을 것 같아요. 내일 올게요.
translation: Um, I'd like to open a savings account. I brought my passport. You need your alien registration card too. A passport alone won't do. Oh, I didn't bring it today. When I asked at another bank, they said a passport alone was fine. When we checked, we found the registration card is definitely required for savings accounts. Would you come back tomorrow? Yes, when I go home and look, I think it will be in the drawer. I'll come tomorrow.

pattern.title: after trying, I found

pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -아 보니(까) if the last vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ, otherwise -어 보니(까) (먹어 보니까); 하다 becomes 해 보니(까).

After living in Korea, I found it more comfortable than I expected.

practice.scene: A foreign student wants to open a savings account at the bank and has brought his passport but not his alien registration card. The teller says the card is required and he must decide whether to come back tomorrow.

No. When the vendor cut one for me and I tried it, it was very sweet. It was the same last time too. Really? Then let's go with this one even if it's small. It'll be tasty at the picnic.

paragraph: 할아버지, 세배 받으십시오. 새해 복 많이 받으시고 건강하십시오. 고맙다. 올해는 학교에서 무엇을 하고 싶으냐? 작년에 동아리 활동을 해 보니까 정말 재미있었습니다. 올해도 계속하겠습니다. 그래, 해 보니까 좋은 일은 계속해야 한다. 공부도 열심히 하거라. 자, 세뱃돈이다. 감사합니다, 할아버지. 써 보니까 용돈이 모자랐는데 책을 사는 데 쓰겠습니다.
translation: Grandfather, please receive my New Year bow. Have lots of blessings in the new year and stay healthy. Thank you. What do you want to do at school this year? When I tried club activities last year, they were really fun. I will continue this year too. Yes, things that turn out good when you try them should be continued. Study hard too. Here, your New Year's money. Thank you, Grandfather. When I tried spending, my allowance fell short, so I'll use this to buy books.

paragraph: 안녕하세요! 목요일 6시 반에 고깃집에서 저녁 어때요? 안녕하세요. 그날 치과 예약이 있는데 6시에 끝나요. 6시 반은 좀 빠듯해요. 아, 그렇군요. 제가 가게에 전화해 보니까 7시 반도 자리가 있대요. 괜찮으세요? 네, 좋아요. 지난번에 치과에 가 보니까 치료 후에 시간이 좀 걸리더라고요. 7시 반이 편해요. 그럼 7시 반으로 예약할게요. 목요일에 봐요!
translation: Hello! How about dinner at a Korean BBQ place on Thursday at 6:30? Hello. I have a dentist appointment that day that ends at 6. 6:30 is a bit tight. Oh, I see. When I called the restaurant, they said there's a table at 7:30 too. Is that okay? Yes, good. When I went to the dentist last time, it took a while after treatment. 7:30 is comfortable. Then I'll book for 7:30. See you Thursday!

paragraph: 사장님, 오늘 저녁에 구워 먹게 고등어 한 마리만 주세요. 어쩌죠? 고등어는 오늘 다 팔렸어요. 방금 알려 드리려던 참이었는데 손님이 먼저 말씀하셨네요. 아, 그래요? 저는 다른 가게에 가려던 참이었는데 여기도 없네요. 대신 싱싱한 갈치는 어떠세요? 아침에 들어와서 지금 막 진열하려던 참이에요. 갈치도 구워 먹으면 맛있죠. 그럼 두 마리 주세요.
translation: Boss, please give me just one mackerel to grill for dinner tonight. What should I do? The mackerel is all sold out today. I was just about to tell you, but you spoke first. Oh, really? I was just about to go to another shop, but you don't have it here either. How about fresh cutlassfish instead? It came in this morning, and I was just about to put it on display. Cutlassfish is tasty grilled too. Then give me two, please.

pattern.title: was just about to
pattern.explain: Use -(으)려던 참이다 to say you were right on the point of doing something when something else happened: 하려던 참이에요 = I was just about to do it.

sample.en: I was just about to go

pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -으려던 참이다 after a consonant (먹으려던 참이에요), -려던 참이다 after a vowel (가려던 참이에요).

examples.en: I was just about to call you.
I was just about to eat lunch too.

pattern.note: It means the action was about to start at that very moment, not a general plan.

practice.scene: A customer wants grilled mackerel for dinner, but the fish seller says the mackerel is sold out today. The seller suggests fresh cutlassfish instead, and the customer decides whether to take it.

paragraph: 나 너무 배고파. 난 치라시동 먹으려던 참이야. 나도 그거 시키려던 참이었는데, 2인 세트가 더 이득이야. 세트는 양이 적을 것 같아. 각자 치라시동 시키자. 그럼 세트 하나에 치라시동 하나 추가할까? 나 점원 부르려던 참이야. 좋아, 그렇게 하자. 내가 부르려던 참이었는데 네가 불러.

Let's each order a chirashi bowl. Then shall we add one chirashi bowl to the set? I was just about to call the server. Good, let's do that. I was just about to call, but you do it.

paragraph: 선생님, 저는 5월 10일에 대전에서 작은 결혼식을 올립니다. 오실 수 있으십니까? 축하합니다! 마침 일정을 확인하려던 참이었습니다. 기꺼이 참석하겠습니다. 감사합니다. 사실 청첩장도 보내 드리려던 참이었습니다. 그런데 예식은 몇 시에 시작합니까? 지금 달력에 적어 두려던 참입니다. 오후 2시에 시작합니다. 와 주셔서 정말 감사합니다.

Actually, I was just about to send you the invitation too. By the way, what time does the ceremony start? I was just about to write it in my calendar. It starts at 2 p.m. Thank you so much for coming.

paragraph: 안녕하세요, 회원님. 운동 목표를 여쭤보려던 참이었어요. 어떤 목표가 있으세요? 살을 빼고 싶어요. 그런데 스쿼트를 하면 무릎이 조금 아파요. 사실 말씀드리려던 참이었어요. 그럼 오늘은 스쿼트를 빼려던 참이었는데, 무릎이 언제 아픈지 말씀해 주세요. 깊이 앉으려던 순간에 특히 아파요. 계단을 내려갈 때도 그래요. 알겠습니다. 그럼 무릎에 부담이 적은 유산소부터 시작하겠습니다.

It's the same going down stairs. Understood. Then we'll start with cardio that puts less strain on your knees.

paragraph: 어, 벌써 11시 20분이네요. 막차가 11시 50분인데 안 놓치기를 바라요. 역이 좀 멀어요. 지금 바로 나가시거나 저랑 택시를 타세요. 택시요? 그럼 신세 질게요. 길이 막히지 않기를 바라요. 저도 안 막히기를 바라요. 얼른 가요.
translation: Oh, it's already 11:20. The last train is at 11:50, so I hope I don't miss it. The station is a bit far. Either leave right now or take a taxi with me. A taxi? Then I'll accept your help. I hope the road isn't jammed. I hope it isn't jammed too. Let's go quickly.

pattern.title: hope that
pattern.explain: Use -기(를) 바라다 to wish good things for someone: 잘 보기를 바라요 = I hope you do well.
pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -기를 바라다, regardless of a final consonant (먹기를 바라요, 가기를 바라요). The 를 can be dropped.

examples.en: I hope you do well on the exam.
I wish that everyone be happy.

pattern.note: It is rather formal; 바라요 and 바랍니다 are common in speeches, letters and notices.

practice.scene: At a housewarming party in Mapo, A realizes the last subway is at 11:50 and it is already 11:20. B, a new acquaintance, says the station is far and suggests A leave now or take a taxi with B.

paragraph: 엄마, 저 오늘 좀 늦을 것 같아요. 팀 회의가 길어졌거든요. 또? 일찍 끝내자고 말해 봤자 소용없겠구나. 밥은 먹었니? 아직요. 회의 끝나고 먹을게요. 지금 빨리 먹어 봤자 체할 것 같아요. 그래도 뭐라도 먹어. 굶고 일해 봤자 능률만 떨어져. 알겠어요. 샌드위치라도 사 먹을게요.
translation: Mom, I think I'll be late today. Our team meeting ran long. Again? I guess there's no use telling them to finish early. Have you eaten? Not yet. I'll eat after the meeting. Even if I eat quickly now, I'd probably get indigestion. Still, eat something. Even if you work hungry, it's no use, your efficiency just drops. Okay. I'll at least buy and eat a sandwich.

translation: What shall we eat for dinner? Do you want to go to the samgyeopsal place by home, or eat tteokbokki at the market? I have a cold. They say sweating is good for colds. Even if we go to the market the line will be long, but I still want to eat it. Okay. I'll go buy it and come back. You rest at home.

Even if I stay longer than that, I'll be hungry and miserable. Okay, let's do that. Right after, let's go eat breakfast.

paragraph: 선생님, 칠판이 잘 안 보여요. 앞으로 옮기면 안 될까요? 네, 한 자리가 비어 있어요. 그런데 창문 옆이라서 밝을 거예요. 괜찮아요. 눈이 나빠서 뒤에 앉으면 안 돼요. 그럼 거기에 앉으세요. 하지만 햇빛 때문에 졸면 안 돼요! 네, 안 졸게요.

pattern.title: must not

translation: Excuse me. Why is the flight to Jeju delayed? I'm sorry, sir. Departure is delayed because of heavy snow and strong wind. For safety, we have to wait a little longer. I see. When can I get another update? We will update you again in one hour. Until then, you need to stay near here. Understood. I will wait.

pattern.title: have to
pattern.explain: Use -아야/어야 하다 to say something must be done or should be done: 일어나야 해요 = I have to get up.
pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -아야 하다 after ㅏ or ㅗ (가야 하다), -어야 하다 after other vowels (먹어야 하다), 해야 하다 for 하다.

examples.en: I have to get up early tomorrow.
You must take the medicine every day.

pattern.note: Past is 해야 했어요, not 해야 하았어요; -아야/어야 되다 is a common, slightly more casual equivalent.

practice.scene: At Incheon Airport, a traveler asks a check-in staff member why the flight to Jeju is delayed. The staff member explains that heavy snow and strong wind are causing the delay and that the next update will come in an hour.

paragraph: 오늘은 첫 시간이니까 목표부터 이야기해 볼까요? 살을 빼고 싶어요. 그런데 스쿼트를 하면 무릎이 조금 아파요. 그러면 무릎을 다치지 않게 자세부터 확인할 필요가 있어요. 그럼 스쿼트를 깊이 할 필요는 없나요? 네, 처음에는 너무 깊이 앉을 필요가 없어요. 아프면 바로 말씀해 주세요.

Then we need to check your form first so you don't hurt your knees. Then is there no need to do squats deeply? Right, at first there's no need to sit too deep. If it hurts, please tell me right away.

pattern.title: need to / no need to
pattern.explain: Use -(으)ㄹ 필요가 있다/없다 to say whether something is needed: 할 필요가 없어요 = there's no need to do it.
pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -을 필요가 있다/없다 after a consonant (읽을 필요가 있다), -ㄹ 필요가 있다/없다 after a vowel (갈 필요가 없다).

examples.ko: 이 일은 지금 당장 할 필요가 없어요.
examples.en: There is no need to do this right now.
examples.rom: i ireun jigeum dangjang hal pillyoga eopseoyo

examples.ko: 발표 전에 자료를 한 번 더 확인할 필요가 있어요.
examples.en: You need to check the materials once more before the presentation.

pattern.note: With 없다 it means 'no need to', not 'must not'; for prohibition use -(으)면 안 되다.

practice.scene: A trainer is leading a first personal training session and asks about the client's goals and any knee pain. The client wants to lose weight but says squats hurt a little.

paragraph: 팀장님이 목요일 회의를 수요일 오전 10시로 옮긴대. 정말? 그때 나 치과 예약이 있는데. 온라인으로 참석해도 될까? 아마 될 거야. 꼭 사무실에 올 필요는 없을 것 같아. 다행이다. 그래도 팀장님께 먼저 물어볼 필요가 있겠지? 응, 내가 확인해 볼게. 네가 따로 말할 필요 없어.
translation: The manager says the Thursday meeting is moved to Wednesday at 10 a.m. Really? I have a dentist appointment then. Could I attend online? Probably. paragraph: 아저씨, 쌀하고 감자를 샀는데 너무 무거워요. 저녁까지 아파트로 배달해 주실 수 있어요? 네, 가능해요. 배달비는 오천 원이고, 여섯 시까지 가요. 다행이에요. 무거운 봉지를 들고 가면 넘어지기 쉬워서 걱정했어요. 맞아요, 짐이 많으면 넘어지기 쉬워요. 그리고 감자는 상하기 쉬우니까 시원한 곳에 두세요. 네, 그럴게요. 감사합니다!
translation: Sir, I bought rice and potatoes and they're too heavy. Could you deliver them to my apartment by this evening? Yes, that's possible. The delivery fee is 5,000 won, and we'll get there by six o'clock. What a relief. I was worried because it's easy to fall if I carry heavy bags. That's right, it's easy to fall when you have lots of bags. And potatoes spoil easily, so keep them in a cool place. Yes, I will. Thank you!

paragraph: 안녕하세요. 예약은 못 했는데 세 명 자리 있어요? 죄송해요. 지금 15분 정도 기다리셔야 해요. 바 자리에 앉으시는 게 좋겠어요. 바 자리요? 일곱 시라서 사람이 많네요. 기다리는 게 좋겠죠? 배가 고프시면 바 자리에 앉는 편이 좋아요. 김치찌개는 금방 나와요. 그럼 바 자리로 할게요. 세 명이 앉을 수 있죠?
translation: Hello. I couldn't make a reservation, but do you have a table for three? I'm sorry. You'll have to wait about 15 minutes right now. It would be better to sit at the bar. The bar? Please make the reservation.

I'll have the driver call you.

paragraph: 어, 카드에 잔액이 없네요. 현금으로 내도 돼요? 현금은 정확한 금액만 받아요. 거스름돈은 못 드려요. 천 원짜리밖에 없는데... 바쁘면 충전을 깜빡하기 마련이죠. 맞아요. 누구나 그런 실수를 하기 마련이에요. 그래도 해결해야 출발할 수 있어요. 잠시만요, 동전이 있는지 찾아볼게요.

pattern.meaning: is bound to; naturally tends to
pattern.title: bound to
pattern.explain: Use -기 마련이다 to say something naturally happens or is sure to happen: 실수하기 마련이에요 = (people) are bound to make mistakes.

examples.en: Everyone is bound to make mistakes.

pattern.note: Describes a natural or general truth, not a one-time event or personal obligation.

practice.scene: A rider's transit card has no balance left at the bus fare reader, and the driver says the bus can't leave until it's sorted. The rider asks if they can pay with cash, but the driver says cash is only accepted with exact change.

paragraph: 여러분, 박물관은 여섯 시에 문을 닫습니다. 구경하다 보면 시간이 빨리 가기 마련이니 확인해 주십시오. 알겠습니다. 어디에서 모일까요? 오디오 가이드는 요금이 따로 있습니까? 로비에서 다섯 시 오십 분에 모이겠습니다. 오디오 가이드는 무료입니다. 도자기실에서는 사진을 찍을 수 없습니다. 보면 찍고 싶어지기 마련이지만 참아 주십시오. 네, 감사합니다.
translation: Everyone, the museum closes at six. When you look around, time is bound to go quickly, so please check. Understood. Where should we gather? Is there a separate fee for the audio guide? We will gather in the lobby at 5:50. The audio guide is free. Photos are not allowed in the ceramics room. You are bound to want to take them when you see the pieces, but please refrain. Yes, thank you.

paragraph: 내일 토요일인데 한강으로 피크닉 갈래요? 좋죠! 그런데 아침에 이사를 해야 해서 네 시 넘어서 갈 수 있어요. 이사하는 날은 정신없기 마련인데 괜찮겠어요? 피곤하기 마련이지만 그래도 가고 싶어요. 그럼 네 시에 한강에서 만나요.
translation: Tomorrow is Saturday, want to go on a picnic to the Han River? Sounds good! But I have to move in the morning, so I can only go after four. Moving day is bound to be hectic, will you be okay? I'm bound to be tired, but I still want to go. Then let's meet at the Han River at four.

paragraph: 선배님, 프린터에 종이가 걸려서 보고서가 안 나와요. 3시 회의 전에 꼭 해 내야 하는데 어떡하죠? 걱정 마세요. 뒤쪽 뚜껑을 열고 걸린 종이를 천천히 당겨 보세요. 아, 나왔어요! 스무 쪽을 다 출력해 냈어요. 감사합니다. 잘 해 내셨네요. 회의 잘하세요.
translation: Sunbae, paper is jammed in the printer so my report won't come out. I have to get it done before the 3 o'clock meeting, what do I do? Don't worry. Open the back cover and slowly try pulling out the stuck paper. Oh, it came out! I managed to print all twenty pages. Thank you. You managed it well. Good luck with the meeting.

pattern.meaning: manage to do; accomplish through effort
pattern.title: manage to do
pattern.explain: Use -아/어 내다 to say you finished something difficult through effort: 참아 냈어요 = I managed to endure it.
pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -아 내다 after the vowel ㅏ or ㅗ (찾아 내다), -어 내다 after other vowels (참아 내다 is ㅏ; 이겨 내다 is 이기다 → 이겨). Use the 해 form for 하다 verbs (해 내다).

pattern.note: It implies effort and difficulty overcome, so it sounds odd with easy, effortless actions.

practice.scene: A new employee can't get the office printer to print her 20-page report because paper is jammed, and asks a colleague who sits nearby to show her how to fix it before a 3 p.m. meeting.

paragraph: 와, 초콜릿 케이크다! 한 조각 먹어도 돼? 잠깐, 그거 땅콩 들어갔어. 너 알레르기 있잖아. 방금 겨우 기억해 냈어. 고마워! 큰일 날 뻔했네. 땅콩 안 들어간 건 없어? 과일 타르트 있어. 견과류는 하나도 안 들어갔어. 좋아! 케이크 냄새가 너무 좋아서 참아 내기 힘들었는데 타르트 먹을게. 그래, 잘 참아 냈네. 많이 먹어!
translation: Wow, chocolate cake! Can I have a slice? Wait, that has peanuts in it. You're allergic, right? I just barely managed to remember. Thanks! That was a close call. Is there anything without peanuts? There's a fruit tart. It has no nuts at all. Great! The cake smelled so good that it was hard to hold back, so I'll have the tart. Yeah, you held out well. Eat a lot!

paragraph: 다음 주 금요일 면접 때 입을 첫 양복을 사려고 합니다. 어떤 색과 디자인이 단정해 보입니까? 차콜색 정장을 추천드립니다. 어두운 회색이라 신뢰감을 줍니다. 수선에는 사흘이 걸립니다. 사흘이면 금요일 전에 받을 수 있겠군요. 면접을 잘 해 내고 싶습니다. 이 정장이면 충분히 좋은 인상을 만들어 내실 수 있습니다. 긴장되지만 끝까지 잘 해 내겠습니다. 이걸로 하겠습니다.
translation: I'm going to buy my first suit to wear to my interview next Friday. What color and design look neat and professional? I recommend a charcoal suit. Being dark gray, it gives an impression of trustworthiness. Alterations take three days. With three days I can get it before Friday. I want to get through the interview well. With this suit you can certainly create a good impression. I'm nervous, but I will manage it well to the end. I'll take this one.

paragraph: 저기요, 이 2호선 열차 강남 가는 거 맞죠? 홍대에서 탔는데 신촌 쪽으로 가는 것 같아요. 아, 반대 방향이에요. 다음 역에서 내려서 건너편 승강장으로 가세요. 아, 감사합니다. 외국인이라 길을 혼자 찾아 내기 어려웠어요. 표지판에 강남 방면이라고 써 있어요. 그걸 따라가면 잘 찾아 내실 거예요. 네, 이번에는 제대로 찾아 낼게요. 도와주셔서 감사합니다.
translation: Excuse me, this Line 2 train goes to Gangnam, right? I got on at Hongdae but it seems to be heading toward Sinchon. Oh, it's the opposite direction. Get off at the next station and go to the platform across the way. Oh, thank you. Being a foreigner, it was hard to find my way alone. The signs say Gangnam direction. If you follow them, you'll manage to find it fine. Yes, this time I'll manage to find it properly. Thank you for helping me.

paragraph: 저기요, N서울타워는 어느 길로 가야 해요? 왼쪽 길이 더 짧은데 많이 가팔라요. 가팔라도 시간이 없어서 그 길로 가지 않을 수 없어요. 그럼 천천히 올라가세요. 경치가 좋아서 사진을 찍지 않을 수 없을 거예요. 감사합니다! 덕분에 살았어요.
translation: Excuse me, which path should I take to get to N Seoul Tower? The left path is shorter, but it's very steep. Even if it's steep, I don't have time, so I can't help but take that path. Then go up slowly. The view is so good that you won't be able to help taking photos. Thank you! You saved me.

It's a black leather wallet, and my ID is inside, so I can't help but find it. I checked, and it has been received. You can pick it up at Seoul Station tomorrow. Thank you. Without my ID it's inconvenient, so I can't help but go tomorrow morning.

pattern.title: and then
pattern.explain: Use -아서/어서 when the first action leads into the next one: 만나서 봤어요 = met and then watched.

pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -는 동안, after a vowel or a consonant; ㄹ-stems drop ㄹ (살다 → 사는 동안).

examples.en: While I cooked, my younger sibling cleaned.

examples.en: While living in Korea, I made many friends.

practice.scene: A patient tells the doctor she has had a fever and a cough since Monday, and that the over-the-counter medicine did not help. The doctor asks about other symptoms and says she should take a test.

paragraph: 미안해, 지하철이 신호 때문에 멈췄어. 20분 늦을 것 같아. 괜찮아. 네가 오는 동안 먼저 주문하고 있을게. 기다리는 동안 심심하지? 진짜 미안해. 아니야, 네가 오는 동안 책 읽고 있을게. 천천히 와.
translation: Sorry, the subway stopped because of a signal problem. I think I'll be 20 minutes late. It's okay. I'll order first while you're on your way. Are you bored while waiting? I'm really sorry. No, I'll read a book while you come. Come slowly.

paragraph: 오래 기다리셨습니까? 먼저 음료는 무엇으로 드시겠습니까? 아닙니다. 따뜻한 차로 마시겠습니다. 감사합니다. 이전 회사에서 일하는 동안 어떤 일을 맡으셨습니까? 일하는 동안 주로 고객 상담과 보고서 작성을 맡았습니다. 좋습니다. 면접을 기다리는 동안 편하게 말씀하십시오. 배려해 주셔서 감사합니다. 대화하는 동안 많이 배우겠습니다.
translation: Have you been waiting long? First, what would you like to drink? No. I'll have hot tea. Thank you. What work did you take on while working at your previous company? While working there, I mainly handled customer consultation and report writing. Good. While you wait for the interview, please feel free to talk. Thank you for your consideration. I will learn a lot while we talk.

paragraph: 엄마, 오늘 팀 회의가 길어져서 늦을 것 같아요. 그래요? 그런데 밥은 먹었어요? 아직요. 점심을 먹은 지 여섯 시간이 됐어요. 여섯 시간이나 됐어요? 얼른 뭐라도 먹어요. 네, 먹을게요. 회사에 들어온 지 두 달이 됐지만 아직 야근은 힘들어요.
translation: Mom, today's team meeting ran long, so I think I'll be late. Really? By the way, have you eaten? Not yet. It's been six hours since I ate lunch. It's been six whole hours? Hurry and eat something. Yes, I'll eat. It's been two months since I joined the company, but overtime is still hard.

pattern.title: it's been … since
pattern.explain: Use -(으)ㄴ 지 N이/가 되다 to say how long it has been since something happened: 온 지 일 년 = a year since I came.
pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -은 지 after a consonant, -ㄴ 지 after a vowel, followed by a time expression + 이/가 되다. ㄹ-stems drop ㄹ (살다 → 산 지).

examples.ko: 한국에 온 지 일 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been a year since I came to Korea.
examples.rom: hanguge on ji il nyeoni dwaesseoyo

examples.ko: 한국어를 공부한 지 삼 개월이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been three months since I started studying Korean.
examples.rom: hangugeoreul gongbuhan ji sam gaewori dwaesseoyo

pattern.note: 지 is written with a space before it. The verb is always in the past form -(으)ㄴ, even though the sentence describes elapsed time.

practice.scene: A daughter calls her mother to say that she will be home late tonight because her team meeting ran long, and her mother asks whether she has eaten yet.

paragraph: 어서 오십시오. 이 분야에서 일하신 지 얼마나 되셨습니까? 안녕하십니까. 이 분야에서 일한 지 삼 년이 되었습니다. 그렇군요. 커피를 드시겠습니까, 아니면 차를 드시겠습니까? 감사합니다. 따뜻한 차로 부탁드립니다. 지원서를 낸 지 2주가 되었는데 이렇게 뵙게 되어 영광입니다.

paragraph: 벌써 12시 반이에요. 회사에서 나온 지 30분이 됐어요. 맞아요. 1시까지 돌아가야 하니까 두 곳만 빨리 보고 가요. 좋아요. 마음에 드는 코트가 없어도 바로 돌아가요. 네, 저도 코트를 찾아본 지 한 달이 됐는데 아직 못 샀어요.

Even if there's no coat I like, let's head right back. Yes, it's been a month since I started looking for a coat too, and I still haven't bought one.

paragraph: 체크아웃할게요. 인천공항까지 갈 택시를 불러 주세요. 네, 손님. 택시는 십오 분쯤 걸려요. 그동안 기념품을 사 올게요. 가방을 한 시간만 맡아 주실 수 있어요? 물론이죠. 근처 시장은 물건이 싸기도 하고 예쁘기도 해요. 좋네요. 저는 선물 고르는 게 힘들기도 하고 즐겁기도 해요. 여기 가방표예요. 가방에 붙이세요.
translation: I'd like to check out. Please call a taxi to Incheon Airport. Yes, ma'am. The taxi takes about fifteen minutes. I'll go buy souvenirs in the meantime. Could you keep my suitcase for just an hour? Of course. The market nearby has things that are both cheap and pretty. Sounds good. For me, picking out gifts is both hard and fun. Here is your luggage tag. Please attach it to the suitcase.

pattern.title: both…and, sometimes…sometimes
pattern.explain: Use -기도 하고 -기도 하다 to list two things you do: 보기도 하고 하기도 해요 = sometimes watch, sometimes do.
pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -기도 하고, repeated with a second stem + -기도 하다, with no change after a vowel or a consonant.

examples.ko: 주말에는 영화를 보기도 하고 운동을 하기도 해요.
examples.en: On weekends I sometimes watch movies and sometimes exercise.
examples.rom: jumareneun yeonghwareul bogido hago undongeul hagido haeyo

examples.ko: 그 식당은 맛있기도 하고 싸기도 해요.
examples.en: That restaurant is both tasty and cheap.
examples.rom: geu sikdangeun masitgido hago ssagido haeyo

pattern.note: Both parts should use the same form, and 하다 at the end takes the tense.

practice.scene: A guest checking out asks the clerk to call a taxi to Incheon Airport and to keep her suitcase for an hour while she buys souvenirs. The clerk says the taxi takes about fifteen minutes and gives her a luggage tag.

paragraph: 오빠, 짬뽕 한 입만 먹어 봐도 돼? 응, 먹어 봐. 으악, 너무 매워! 입이 아프기도 하고 눈물이 나기도 해. 그 집 짬뽕은 맵기도 하고 짜기도 해. 탕수육을 시키는 게 어때? 좋아! 탕수육은 달기도 하고 바삭하기도 해서 좋아. 그래, 내가 시킬게. 물부터 마셔.

How about ordering sweet and sour pork? Good! Sweet and sour pork is both sweet and crispy, so I like it. Okay, I'll order it. Drink some water first.

pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -자마자, with no change after a vowel or a consonant (오다 → 오자마자, 먹다 → 먹자마자).

examples.en: I took a shower as soon as I got home.
I met my friend as soon as class ended.

pattern.note: Do not put a tense marker (-았/었-) before -자마자; the tense goes on the final verb.

practice.scene: A job candidate meets a department manager at a café near the office before a second interview. The manager asks about the candidate's experience and what drink they would like, while the candidate answers carefully and thanks them.

paragraph: 저기요, 벤치프레스 몇 세트 남았어요? 두 세트 남았어요. 번갈아 가면서 하실래요? 좋아요. 한 세트가 끝나자마자 제가 들어갈게요. 네, 제가 일어나자마자 바로 하세요. 무게는 알려 주시는 대로 맞춰 드릴게요.
translation: Excuse me, how many sets of bench press do you have left? Two sets left. Would you like to alternate sets? Sounds good. I'll step in as soon as a set finishes. Sure, go right ahead as soon as I get up. I'll adjust the weight as soon as you tell me.

paragraph: 엄마, 오늘 팀 회의가 길어져서 늦을 것 같아요. 그래요? 저녁은 먹었어요? 아직요. 점심도 거른 채 계속 회의만 했어요. 저런, 굶은 채로 그렇게 오래 있으면 안 돼요. 뭐라도 먹고 와요. 네, 가방을 멘 채로 편의점에 들러서 김밥이라도 먹을게요.
translation: Mom, our team meeting is running long today, so I think I'll be late. Is that so? Have you eaten dinner? Not yet. I skipped lunch too and just kept having the meeting. Oh dear, you shouldn't stay that long hungry. Eat something before you come. Okay, I'll stop by a convenience store with my bag still on and at least eat some gimbap.

pattern.title: while staying that way
pattern.explain: Use -(으)ㄴ 채(로) to say you did something while leaving something in the same state: 불을 켠 채로 = with the light left on.
pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -은 채(로) after a consonant, -ㄴ 채(로) after a vowel, with the verb in the past form (켜다 → 켠 채).

examples.en: I fell asleep with the light on.
I went into the room with my shoes on.

pattern.note: It is used with verbs whose result state continues; it is not used for two actions happening at the same time.

practice.scene: A daughter calls her mother to say that she will be home late tonight because her team meeting ran long, and her mother asks whether she has eaten yet.

paragraph: 우리 과학 발표 주제 뭐로 할까? 재활용이랑 태양에너지 중에. 난 재활용이 사진 찾기 더 쉬울 것 같아. 쓰레기가 버려진 채 쌓여 있는 사진이 많잖아. 맞아. 태양에너지는 지붕에 패널이 설치된 채 찍은 사진뿐이라 다 비슷해. 그럼 재활용으로 하자. 내가 오늘 밤에 사진 모아 볼게. 좋아. 나는 발표 자료를 만들어 볼게.
translation: What should we pick for our science presentation topic? Recycling or solar energy. I think recycling is easier for finding pictures. There are lots of pictures of trash piled up left abandoned. True. For solar energy there are only pictures taken of panels left installed on roofs, so they all look alike. Then let's go with recycling. I'll try collecting pictures tonight. Great. I'll try making the presentation materials.

paragraph: 어서 오십시오. 코트를 입은 채로 앉으셔도 됩니다. 이전 회사에서는 어떤 일을 하셨습니까? 감사합니다. 마케팅 팀에서 삼 년간 일했습니다. 그러셨군요. 음료는 무엇을 드시겠습니까? 따뜻한 차를 부탁드립니다. 준비한 자료는 가방에 넣은 채로 가져왔습니다. 필요하시면 보여 드리겠습니다. 알겠습니다. 제가 주문하고 오겠습니다. 잠시 기다려 주십시오.
translation: Welcome. You may sit with your coat on. What kind of work did you do at your previous company? Thank you. I worked in a marketing team for three years. I see. What would you like to drink? A warm tea, please. I brought the materials I prepared still in my bag. If you need them, I will show you. Understood. I will go order and come back. Please wait a moment.

paragraph: 여보세요, 나 지금 은행 앞에 서 있어. 네가 말한 카페가 어디야? 오빠, 거기서 꽃집을 지나서 두 번째 골목에서 왼쪽으로 돌아. 전화를 끊지 않은 채 걸어와. 내가 말해 줄게. 알았어. 꽃집은 지났어. 이제 첫 번째 골목이야. 응, 하나 더 지나서 돌면 돼. 문을 활짝 연 채 장사하는 카페야. 아, 보인다. 금방 들어갈게.

It's a cafe that does business with its door wide open. Ah, I see it. I'll go in soon.

paragraph: 여보세요? 죄송해요, 제가 지금 버스라서 이따가 다시 전화할게요. 왜요? 옆 사람이 조용히 해 달라고 했어요? 네, 아주 정중하게 말씀하셔서 더 민망했어요. 하하, 그럴 줄 알았어요. 참, 부장님이 내일 회의는 점심도 먹을 겸 친목도 다질 겸 식당에서 한대요. 아, 그래요? 그럼 내일 자세히 얘기해요.
translation: Hello? Sorry, I'm on the bus right now, so I'll call you back later. Why? Did the person next to you ask you to keep it down? Yes, they said it so politely that I was even more embarrassed. Haha, I figured. Oh, the boss said tomorrow's meeting will be at a restaurant, both to have lunch and to build team bonds. Oh, really? Then let's talk in detail tomorrow.

pattern.title: to do both… and…
pattern.explain: Use -(으)ㄹ 겸 to say you do something for two purposes at once: 운동도 할 겸 = to get some exercise too.
pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -을 겸 after a consonant, -ㄹ 겸 after a vowel. It is often paired as -(으)ㄹ 겸 -(으)ㄹ 겸, or used as N 겸 N.

examples.en: I walked there to get some exercise too.
I went to the park partly to get some fresh air.

pattern.note: It states more than one purpose for an action, and the main clause usually has a movement or action verb.

practice.scene: A woman on the bus tells her coworker on a call that she'll call back, because a passenger next to her just asked her politely to keep her voice down. A coworker teases her and says what the boss told everyone about tomorrow's meeting.

I'll treat you, partly to apologize.

paragraph: 체크아웃할게요. 인천공항까지 가는 택시를 불러 주실 수 있어요? 네, 손님. 지금 부르면 택시가 십오 분쯤 걸려요. 그런데 기념품을 좀 사고 싶어서요. 이 가방을 한 시간만 맡아 주세요. 물론이죠. 여기 짐표예요. 이 호텔은 공항에서 가까울 뿐만 아니라 근처에 기념품 가게도 많아서 편하실 거예요. 맞아요. 방이 깨끗할 뿐만 아니라 직원분들도 친절해서 정말 좋았어요.

pattern.title: not only… but also

pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -을 뿐만 아니라 after a consonant, -ㄹ 뿐만 아니라 after a vowel. With nouns, use N뿐만 아니라 or N일 뿐만 아니라.

examples.en: This restaurant's food is not only tasty but also cheap.

pattern.note: The second clause adds a similar point and usually takes 도.

paragraph: 조금만 더 가자. 이 길로 한 바퀴만 돌면 끝이야. 언니, 나 못 걷겠어. 새 신발이 불편할 뿐만 아니라 발도 너무 아파. 아까 벤치에서 쉬었잖아. 오늘 날씨가 좋은 데다가 단풍도 예쁜데 아깝지 않아? 예쁘긴 한데 나는 지금 앉고 싶어. 다리도 아플 뿐만 아니라 목도 말라. 알았어. 저기 카페까지만 가자. 거기서 앉아서 마시자.
translation: Let's go a little more. If we just go around this path once, we're done. Sis, I can't walk. Not only are my new shoes uncomfortable, but my feet really hurt too. Just open this cover and slowly pull out the jammed paper. Try it once. Wow, it's coming out! Not only is it easy, it's fast. Thank you so much.

Then while you're setting up, could you get the coffee too? Yes, okay. Let's talk later then.

pattern.title: because (of the fact)
pattern.explain: Use -기 때문에 to state a reason in a clear, slightly firm way: 비가 오기 때문에 = because it is raining.
pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -기 때문에, with no change after a vowel or a consonant. After a noun use N 때문에, or N(이)기 때문에.

examples.en: We canceled the picnic because it is raining.

examples.ko: 길이 막히기 때문에 저는 지하철을 타요.
examples.en: Because the roads get jammed, I take the subway.
examples.rom: giri makigi ttaemune jeoneun jihacheoreul tayo

pattern.note: It states the reason firmly, and commands and suggestions are not natural in the second clause.

practice.scene: Two close friends are at a mall choosing a dress for one of them to wear to a cousin's wedding on Saturday. One likes the blue dress, the other thinks the green one looks better with her skin tone.

paragraph: 부장님, 급행버스가 길이 막히기 때문에 2시까지 도착하기 어렵습니다. 그렇습니까? 오늘 거래처 회의가 중요하기 때문에 늦으면 안 됩니다. 어떻게 하면 좋겠습니까? 다음 역에서 지하철로 갈아타시면 어떻겠습니까? 지하철은 막히지 않기 때문에 2시 전에 도착할 수 있습니다. 좋습니다. 시간이 별로 없기 때문에 그렇게 합시다. 네, 제가 길을 안내하겠습니다.
translation: Sir, the express bus is stuck in traffic, so it is hard to arrive by 2:00. Is that so? Today's client meeting is important, so we must not be late. What should we do? How about switching to the subway at the next station? The subway doesn't get stuck, so we can arrive before 2:00. Good. We don't have much time, so let's do that. Yes, I will guide the way.

pattern.title: because it is…
pattern.explain: Add N(이)라서 after a noun to say because it is that thing: 휴일이라서 = because it's a holiday.
pattern.attaches: Noun + 이라서 after a consonant (학생이라서), 라서 after a vowel (의사라서).

examples.en: Because today is a holiday, there are many people.
Because I'm a foreigner, Korean is hard for me.

pattern.note: It is the -아서/어서 form of 이다, so it also cannot take commands or suggestions.

practice.scene: A customer asks the cashier for the Wi-Fi password and says the connection keeps dropping. The cashier explains that the password is printed on the receipt and that the signal is weak near the window.

Because it's the weekend, it seems the roads are congested.

translation: I was about to leave, but the manager asked for the report by tomorrow morning. Really? I have dinner plans tonight. Because the deadline is tomorrow morning, there's no choice. After we finish, let's at least eat a late-night snack together.

pattern.title: thanks to
pattern.explain: Use -(으)ㄴ/는 덕분에 to give credit for a good result: 도와주신 덕분에 = thanks to your help.
pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -는 덕분에 (present), or -(으)ㄴ 덕분에 (past: 도와주신 덕분에). Adjective stem + -(으)ㄴ 덕분에 (좋은 덕분에). Noun + 덕분에.

examples.en: Thanks to the teacher's help, I passed the exam.
Thanks to the good weather, the trip was enjoyable.

pattern.note: It is only for positive results, and for negative results use -(으)ㄴ/는 탓에 or -는 바람에.

pattern.title: you see, because
pattern.explain: Add -거든요 to give a reason or background the other person may not know: 바쁘거든요 = you see, I'm busy.

paragraph: 프런트입니다. 무엇을 도와드릴까요? 옆방이 너무 시끄럽습니다. 노느라고 떠드는지 소리가 계속 들려서 잘 수가 없습니다. 정말 죄송합니다. 직원이 다른 일을 처리하느라고 바로 확인하지 못했습니다. 지금 바로 말씀드리겠습니다. 감사합니다. 저도 내일 일찍 일어나야 하는데 계속 깨느라고 너무 피곤합니다. 계속되면 다른 층으로 객실을 옮겨 드리겠습니다. 다시 전화 주십시오.
translation: This is the front desk. How may I help you? The room next door is very loud. They seem to be making noise because they're busy partying, and I can't sleep. I'm very sorry. Our staff was busy handling other things and couldn't check right away. I will speak to them right now. Thank you. I have to get up early tomorrow, and I'm exhausted from being awake the whole time. If it continues, we will move you to a room on another floor. Please call again.

pattern.meaning: because of doing (busy with), often negative result
pattern.title: because I was busy doing
pattern.explain: Use -느라고 to say you were busy doing one thing, so something else didn't work out: 공부하느라고 = busy studying.
pattern.attaches: Action verb stem + -느라고, with no change after a vowel or a consonant (하느라고, 먹느라고). ㄹ-stems keep ㄹ out (놀다 → 노느라고).

examples.en: I couldn't sleep because I was busy studying for the exam.
I couldn't meet my friend because I was busy with my part-time job.

pattern.note: It needs the same subject in both clauses and an action verb, and it cannot be used with commands or suggestions.

practice.scene: A guest calls the front desk at midnight because the room next door is very loud and she cannot sleep. The manager apologizes, promises to talk to them, and offers to move her to another floor if it continues.

paragraph: 실례합니다. 강남 가는 402번 버스를 기다리고 있는데 안 와요. 여기는 402번이 안 서요. 길 건너편으로 가세요. 지도 보느라고 정류장을 잘못 찾으셨나 봐요. 아, 맞아요. 휴대폰 보느라고 표지판을 못 봤어요. 건너편 정류장이 가까워요? 좀 멀어요. 걸어가느라고 시간 쓰는 것보다 지하철을 타는 게 나을 거예요.
translation: Excuse me. I'm waiting for bus 402 to Gangnam, but it doesn't come. Bus 402 doesn't stop here. Go across the street. You must have found the wrong stop because you were busy looking at the map. Ah, right. I was busy looking at my phone and didn't see the sign. Is the stop across the street close? It's a bit far. Taking the subway would be better than spending time walking there.

paragraph: 사장님, 오늘 저녁에 구워 먹게 고등어 있어요? 죄송해요, 오늘은 태풍 때문에 고등어가 다 팔렸어요. 아, 그래요? 그럼 뭐가 좋아요? 싱싱한 갈치가 있어요. 고등어 때문에 오셨죠? 갈치도 구우면 맛있어요. 좋아요. 그럼 갈치 두 마리 주세요.
translation: Boss, do you have mackerel to grill for dinner tonight? Sorry, because of the typhoon the mackerel is all sold out today. Oh, really? Then what's good? We have fresh cutlassfish. You came because of the mackerel, right? Cutlassfish is tasty grilled too. Okay. Then please give me two cutlassfish.

pattern.title: because of
pattern.explain: Add N때문에 after a word to give the reason, often a bad result: 비 때문에 = because of the rain.
pattern.attaches: Attaches directly to a noun, with no change after a vowel or a consonant (비 때문에, 감기 때문에).

examples.en: We couldn't go on the picnic because of the rain.
I didn't come to school because of a cold.

pattern.note: It is often used for negative causes; it cannot be used with a command or suggestion in the second clause naturally.

practice.scene: A customer wants grilled mackerel for dinner, but the fish seller says the mackerel is sold out today. The seller suggests fresh cutlassfish instead, and the customer decides whether to take it.

paragraph: 누나, 혹시 TV 리모컨 못 봤어? 아무리 찾아도 없어. 리모컨? 아침에 소파 쿠션 밑에서 봤어. 아, 여기 있다! 너 때문에 살았다. 그거 때문에 십 분이나 찾았어. 웃기네. 네가 어제 쿠션 때문에 소파 어질러 놓고 안 치웠잖아.
translation: Sis, have you seen the TV remote by any chance? I can't find it no matter how I look. The remote? I saw it under the sofa cushion this morning. Oh, here it is! You saved me. I searched ten minutes because of that thing. That's funny. You left the sofa messy yesterday because of the cushion and didn't tidy up.

paragraph: 여보세요, 예약한 손님입니다. 버스 지연 때문에 8시가 아니라 밤 11시쯤 도착할 것 같습니다. 알겠습니다, 고객님. 저희 프런트는 밤새 운영하니 걱정하지 마십시오. 감사합니다. 늦은 도착 때문에 방이 취소되지는 않겠지요? 그렇지 않습니다. 확인 때문에 여쭙겠습니다. 예약자 성함이 어떻게 되십니까?
translation: Hello, I'm a guest with a reservation. Because of a bus delay, I will arrive around 11 p.m., not 8. Understood, sir. Our front desk is open all night, so please don't worry. Thank you. Because of the late arrival, the room won't be cancelled, will it? It won't. I'm asking for confirmation purposes. What is the name on the booking?

paragraph: 선생님, 앞자리로 옮겨도 돼요? 칠판이 잘 안 보여서요. 눈 때문에 그래요? 한 자리가 비어 있어요. 네, 눈이 나빠서요. 안경 때문에 머리도 아파요. 그런데 창문 옆이라서 햇빛 때문에 밝을 수 있어요. 괜찮아요? 네, 괜찮아요. 밝은 게 더 좋아요.

But it's next to the window, so it may be bright because of the sunlight. Is that okay? Yes, it's fine. Bright is better.

paragraph: 이 곤색 스웨터 있어요? 30% 할인한다고 해서 왔어요. 죄송해요. 곤색은 인기가 많은 나머지 어제 다 팔렸어요. 회색이랑 베이지만 남았어요. 아, 그래요? 기대한 나머지 다른 색은 생각도 못 했어요. 다음 주에 다시 들어오니까 기다리셔도 돼요. 회색도 잘 어울리실 거예요. 고민한 나머지 머리가 아프네요. 그냥 회색으로 할게요.
translation: Do you have this navy sweater? I came because it's 30% off. I'm sorry. The navy was so popular that it all sold out yesterday. Only grey and beige are left. Oh, really? I was so excited that I didn't even think of other colors. It comes back in next week, so you can wait. Grey would suit you well too. I've thought about it so much that my head hurts. I'll just take the grey one.

pattern.title: so much that

pattern.note: It states an excessive degree as the cause of an unintended or negative result; it can't be used for commands or suggestions.

paragraph: 아버지, 에어컨에서 이상한 소리가 납니다. 어제는 너무 시끄러운 나머지 잠을 못 잤습니다. 그랬니? 나는 일에 집중한 나머지 전혀 듣지 못했구나. 수리는 어떻게 하지? 수리 기사님께 전화했더니 목요일에 올 수 있다고 하셨습니다. 목요일 몇 시에 오시니? 가족들은 그때 괜찮겠니? 오후 두 시입니다. 저는 수업이 없고 어머니도 계십니다. 걱정한 나머지 미리 확인했습니다.
translation: Father, the air conditioner is making a strange noise. Yesterday it was so loud that I couldn't sleep. Was it? I was so absorbed in work that I didn't hear it at all. What about the repair? I called the repair technician, and he said he can come on Thursday. What time on Thursday? Will that be fine for the family? It's two in the afternoon. I have no class and Mother will be home. I was so worried that I checked in advance.

I'm in such a rush that I'm asking. The delivery fee is 5,000 won. If I leave now, it arrives around six. Great. My arms hurt from carrying heavy stuff so long, so thank you so much.

paragraph: 어, 벌써 열한 시 이십 분이에요? 대화에 빠진 나머지 시간을 몰랐어요. 막차가 몇 시예요? 여기서 역까지 꽤 멀어요. 열한 시 오십 분이에요. 놀란 나머지 심장이 뛰네요. 지금 바로 나가세요. 아니면 저랑 택시 타요. 저도 같은 방향이에요. 정말요? 걱정한 나머지 아무 생각도 안 났는데 고마워요.
translation: Oh, it's already 11:20? I was so absorbed in talking that I lost track of time. What time is the last train? The station is quite far from here. It's 11:50. I was so startled that my heart is pounding. Leave right now. Or take a taxi with me. I'm going the same way. Really? I was so worried that I couldn't think at all, so thank you.

paragraph: 저기요, 남자 샤워실에 온수가 안 나와요. 죄송해요, 회원님. 어제 보일러를 점검한 탓에 문제가 생긴 것 같아요. 오늘 아침에도 찬물만 나와서 너무 추웠어요. 날씨가 추운 탓에 보일러에 무리가 간 것 같아요. 기술자가 곧 올 거예요. 그동안 2층 샤워실을 이용해 주시겠어요? 네, 그럴게요. 2층으로 갈게요.
translation: Excuse me, there's no hot water in the men's shower. I'm sorry, sir. I think a problem came up because the boiler was inspected yesterday. Only cold water came out this morning too, so I was really cold. I think the boiler is overworked because the weather is cold. A technician will come soon. Would you use the second-floor shower in the meantime? Yes, I will. I'll go to the second floor.

paragraph: 실례합니다. 제주행 비행기가 왜 지연되는지 알 수 있습니까? 현재 제주 지역에 폭설이 내리고 바람도 강하므로 출발이 지연되고 있습니다. 그럼 언제쯤 출발할 수 있습니까? 안전이 가장 중요하므로 정확한 시간은 말씀드리기 어렵습니다. 한 시간 후에 다시 안내해 드리겠습니다.
translation: Excuse me. Can I find out why the flight to Jeju is delayed? Since heavy snow is falling in the Jeju area and the wind is also strong, the departure is being delayed. Then about when can it depart? Since safety is the most important thing, it is difficult to give you an exact time. We will give you another update in one hour.

paragraph: 기사님, 서울역은 이쪽이 아닌 것 같은데요. 손님, 앞에 공사 중이라 길이 막혀 있기에 돌아가는 중이에요. 아, 그렇군요. 저는 길을 잘못 드신 줄 알았어요. 차가 너무 안 가기에 다른 길로 들어섰어요. 그럼 이 길로 가면 많이 늦어요? 아니요, 십 분쯤 더 걸리기에 약속 시간에는 괜찮을 거예요.
translation: Driver, I don't think Seoul Station is this way. Sir, since the road ahead is blocked by construction, I'm taking a detour. Oh, I see. I thought you had taken a wrong turn. Since the cars weren't moving at all, I turned onto another road. Then will it take much longer going this way? No, since it takes only about ten more minutes, you should be fine for your appointment.

pattern.title: seeing that, so
pattern.explain: Use -기에 to say you did something because of what you noticed: 날씨가 좋기에 = seeing the weather was nice.
pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -기에, with no change after a vowel or a consonant (좋기에, 싸기에).

examples.en: The weather was nice, so I went out for a walk.
The price was cheap, so I bought one.

pattern.note: The second clause is the speaker's action in response to what was seen or judged, and it is not used with commands.

practice.scene: A passenger notices the taxi driver is going the wrong way to Seoul Station and complains politely. The driver says the road ahead is blocked, and the passenger asks whether the new route will be much slower.

paragraph: 이쪽 큰길로 가자. 골목은 어두워서 불안해. 아니야, 가게 아저씨가 골목이 빠르다고 하기에 그쪽으로 가려고 했어. 정말? 얼마나 빠르대? 큰길은 신호가 많기에 오 분은 더 걸린대. 그래? 네가 그렇게 자신 있어 하기에 믿어 볼게. 걱정 마. 길이 좁기에 천천히 걸으면 돼.
translation: Let's take this main road. The alley is dark and makes me uneasy. No, since the shopkeeper said the alley is faster, I was going to go that way. Really? How much faster did he say? Since the main road has lots of traffic lights, he said it takes five more minutes. Is that so? Seeing how confident you are, I'll trust you. Don't worry. Since the path is narrow, we just walk slowly.

paragraph: 이사님, 부산에서 가족 결혼식이 있기에 금요일과 월요일에 휴가를 내고 싶습니다. 결혼식이라면 가야지요. 그런데 금요일 고객사 전화는 누가 받습니까? 박 대리가 그날 시간이 된다고 하기에 부탁해 두었습니다. 자료는 준비되어 있습니까? 네, 어제 정리해 놓았기에 박 대리가 바로 볼 수 있습니다. 알겠습니다. 잘 다녀오십시오.

Since Assistant Manager Park said he is available that day, I have already asked him. Are the materials ready? Yes, since I organized them yesterday, Assistant Manager Park can look at them right away. Understood. Have a good trip.

paragraph: 과학 발표 주제 정했어? 재활용이랑 태양에너지 중에 고민 중이야. 나는 재활용이 좋을 것 같아. 사진이 많기에 자료 만들기 쉬울 거야. 태양에너지는 어때? 어제 찾아봤는데 사진이 별로 없기에 좀 걱정됐어. 그렇구나. 우리 동네 분리수거장 사진도 찍으면 되기에 재활용이 더 편해. 좋아, 네가 그렇게 말하기에 재활용으로 정할게. 잘 생각했어. 오늘 방과 후에 같이 사진 찍으러 가자.
translation: Did you pick the science presentation topic? I'm torn between recycling and solar energy. I think recycling is good. Since we can also take photos of our neighborhood recycling area, recycling is more convenient. Okay, since you say so, I'll settle on recycling. Good call. Let's go take photos together after school today.

paragraph: 저기요, 치즈 떡볶이를 시켰는데 매운 떡볶이가 나왔어요. 죄송합니다, 손님. 주문서에 매운맛이라고 적혀 있길래 그대로 만들었는데 제가 잘못 봤나 봐요. 아이가 한 입 먹고 울길래 제가 먹어 봤더니 너무 매웠어요. 정말 죄송해요. 지금 바로 다시 만들어 드릴게요. 10분만 기다려 주시겠어요? 네, 기다릴게요.

paragraph: 하늘 좀 봐. 구름이 엄청 까매졌어. 그래도 가자. 저번에도 비가 올 것 같다고 해서 안 갔잖아. 저번엔 우산 안 가져가는 바람에 다 젖었잖아. 나 또 감기 걸리면 어떡해? 하긴, 네가 갑자기 비를 맞는 바람에 일주일이나 아팠지. 그러니까 오늘은 카페에 가자. 한강 보이는 데로. 좋아. 거기서 비 구경하자.
translation: Look at the sky. The clouds have gotten really dark. Let's go anyway. Last time too we didn't go because it looked like rain. Last time I didn't bring an umbrella and got all wet. What if I catch a cold again? True, you got rained on suddenly and were sick for a whole week. So let's go to a cafe today. One with a Han River view. Okay. Let's watch the rain from there.

paragraph: 여보세요, 오늘 예약한 손님입니다. 버스가 늦게 출발하는 바람에 8시까지 도착하지 못할 것 같습니다. 괜찮습니다, 고객님. 몇 시쯤 도착하실 예정이십니까? 11시쯤 도착할 것 같습니다. 고속도로에서 사고가 나는 바람에 길이 많이 막혔습니다. 저희 프런트는 밤새 운영하니 걱정하지 않으셔도 됩니다. 예약하신 성함을 말씀해 주시겠습니까? 김민수입니다. 감사합니다. 조심히 가겠습니다.
translation: Hello, I'm a guest who booked for today. Because the bus left late, I don't think I can arrive by 8. That's fine, sir. About what time do you expect to arrive? I think around 11. An accident happened on the highway, so the road was very congested. Our front desk is open all night, so you need not worry. Could you tell me the name the booking is under? It's Kim Minsu. Thank you. I will be careful on the way.

paragraph: 저기요, 제가 계좌번호를 잘못 보는 바람에 50만 원을 다른 사람에게 보냈어요. 아이고, 많이 놀라셨겠어요. 이체한 시간이 언제였어요? 한 시간 전이에요. 급하게 입력하는 바람에 숫자 하나가 틀렸나 봐요. 저희가 받은 분께 연락해 볼 수는 있어요. 그런데 동의를 받아야 해서 며칠 걸릴 수도 있어요. 알겠어요. 그럼 신청서를 써 볼게요.
translation: Excuse me, I misread the account number and sent 500,000 won to someone else. Oh my, you must be shocked. When did you make the transfer? An hour ago. I entered it in a hurry, so one number must have been wrong. We can try contacting the recipient. But we need their consent, so it may take a few days. I see. Then I'll fill out the application form.

paragraph: 아저씨, 쌀하고 감자를 샀을 때는 괜찮았는데 너무 무거워요. 집이 어디예요? 오늘 저녁까지 배달해 드릴 수 있어요? 네, 가능해요. 배달비는 삼천 원이에요. 집에 있을 때 받으시는 게 좋아요. 여섯 시쯤 갈게요. 여섯 시에는 집에 있을 거예요. 고맙습니다!
translation: Sir, it was fine when I bought the rice and potatoes, but it's too heavy. Where is your home? Can you deliver by this evening? Yes, it's possible. The delivery fee is 3,000 won. It's best to receive it when you're home. I'll come around six. I'll be home at six. Thank you!

pattern.title: when
pattern.explain: Use -(으)ㄹ 때 to say at what time something happens: 시간이 있을 때 = when you have time.
pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -ㄹ 때 after a vowel, -을 때 after a consonant (먹을 때). ㄹ-stems keep ㄹ (놀 때).

examples.en: Please call me when you have time.

examples.ko: 한국에 갈 때 비행기를 탈 거예요.
examples.en: I'll take a plane when I go to Korea.
examples.rom: hanguge gal ttae bihaenggireul tal geoyeyo

pattern.note: The tense of the main verb shows whether the time is past or future, and -았/었을 때 means 'when/after it happened'.

practice.scene: A shopper's bags are too heavy after buying rice and potatoes, so she asks a nearby delivery stall worker if they can deliver to her apartment by this evening. He tells her the fee and the delivery time.

It's hard when you're tired and cannot sleep. If the noise continues, we will move you to a room on another floor. Understood. I'll call again when necessary.

paragraph: 전세 대출을 받으실 때 금리가 중요합니다. 두 상품을 비교해 보십시오. A 상품은 금리가 낮지만 갚을 때 부담이 큽니까? 네, 갚을 때 수수료가 있습니다. B 상품은 금리가 높을 때도 수수료가 없습니다. 그러면 B 상품이 좋겠습니다. 다음 주에 올 때 무엇을 가져올까요? 올 때 신분증과 계약서, 소득 증명서를 가져오십시오.
translation: The interest rate is important when you take a deposit loan. Please compare the two products. Product A has a low rate, but is the burden big when we repay? Yes, there's a fee when repaying. Product B has no fee even when the rate is high. Then Product B seems good. What should we bring when we come next week? When you come, please bring ID, the contract, and proof of income.

paragraph: 약사님, 이 약은 하루에 몇 번 먹어요? 하루에 세 번, 식사 후에 드세요. 배가 아프면 밥을 먹고 바로 드세요. 알겠어요. 커피를 마시면 안 돼요? 약을 먹는 동안에는 커피를 마시면 속이 더 안 좋을 수 있어요. 목이 마르면 물을 드세요.
translation: Pharmacist, how many times a day do I take this medicine? Three times a day, after meals. If your stomach hurts, take it right after eating. I see. Is it not okay if I drink coffee? While you're taking the medicine, drinking coffee can upset your stomach more. If you're thirsty, drink water.

pattern.title: if, when
pattern.explain: Add -(으)면 to say what happens if or when something takes place: 비가 오면 = if it rains.
pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -으면 after a consonant (먹으면), -면 after a vowel (가면). 있다 becomes 있으면, and ㄹ-stems drop ㄹ before ㅁ-type endings, so 살다 becomes 살면.

examples.en: If it rains, I will stay home.
If you have time, let's watch a movie together.

pattern.note: Don't put a past or future tense marker before -(으)면 in simple conditions; use the tense in the main clause.

practice.scene: After a visit, a patient asks the pharmacist how often to take the three pills and whether it is okay to drink coffee. The pharmacist explains to take them after meals, three times a day, and to avoid coffee.

paragraph: 지연아, 토요일에 비가 많이 온대. 내일 일기예보 보면 알겠지만 한강 소풍은 취소될 수도 있어. 정말? 너무 아쉽다. 비가 오면 소풍은 못 가네. 응, 비가 많이 오면 위험해서 안 돼. 그럼 비가 오면 영화 보러 가자. 오빠가 시간 되면 같이 가!
translation: Jiyeon, they say it will rain a lot on Saturday. If you check tomorrow's forecast you'll see, but the Han River picnic might be canceled. Really? What a shame. If it rains, we can't go on the picnic. Yeah, if it rains a lot it's dangerous, so no. Then if it rains, let's go see a movie. If you have time, come with me!

translation: We only have an hour for lunch. What if we look for a coat and are late at 1 o'clock? Don't worry. We just need to quickly look at two shops. Okay. paragraph: 저기요, 방금 지하철에 우산을 두고 내렸어요. 어떻게 해야 해요? 먼저 우산 모양을 설명해 주셔야 해요. 그리고 분실물 신청서도 써야 찾을 수 있어요. 검은색 장우산이고 손잡이가 갈색이에요. 신청서는 여기에 쓰면 돼요? 네, 연락처도 정확히 적어야 연락드릴 수 있어요. 종점에서 발견될 수도 있어요.
translation: Excuse me, I just got off the subway and left my umbrella on the train. What should I do? First you need to describe the umbrella. And only if you fill in a lost-and-found form can we look for it. It's a black long umbrella with a brown handle. Do I write the form here? Yes, I can contact you only if you write your phone number accurately too. It may be found at the last stop.

pattern.explain: Use -아야/어야 to say something is needed before a result can happen: 공부해야 = only if you study.
pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -아야 after the vowels ㅏ/ㅗ (가야), -어야 after other vowels (먹어야), and 하다 becomes 해야. Irregular stems change as usual (듣다 becomes 들어야).

paragraph: 구름이 엄청 어두워졌다. 그래도 한강에 가야 해, 오늘 걷기로 했잖아. 비 오면 어떡해? 우산도 없는데. 비를 맞지 않아야 감기도 안 걸리지. 조금만 걸으면 돼. 날씨가 좋아야 산책하는 맛이 나긴 하는데. 그러니까 오늘은 카페에 가자. 비가 그쳐야 나갈 수 있어. 알았어. 대신 커피는 네가 사야 해.

paragraph: 안녕하십니까? 다음 주 금요일 면접 때문에 처음으로 정장을 사려고 합니다. 어서 오십시오. 면접용이라면 단정해 보여야 하니까 차콜색 정장을 추천드립니다. 디자인은 어떤 것이 좋겠습니까? 신뢰감을 줘야 해서 고민입니다. 몸에 잘 맞아야 전문적으로 보이니까 슬림하지 않은 기본 핏이 좋습니다. 수선은 얼마나 걸립니까? 금요일 전에 입어야 합니다. 사흘이 걸립니다. 내일 맡기셔야 금요일 전에 찾으실 수 있습니다.

It takes three days. Only if you leave it tomorrow can you pick it up before Friday.

paragraph: 여보세요, 오늘 아침 2호선에 검은색 지갑을 두고 내렸습니다. 어떻게 해야 합니까? 지갑 모양을 알아야 찾아 드릴 수 있습니다. 브랜드나 안에 든 물건을 말씀해 주십시오. 가죽 반지갑이고 안에 신분증이 있습니다. 혹시 찾으면 어디로 가야 합니까? 내일 서울역 유실물센터로 오십시오. 신분증을 가져오셔야 받으실 수 있습니다.

paragraph: 어서 오십시오. 주택 보증금 대출 상담 때문에 오셨습니까? 네, 고정금리 3.8%와 변동금리 3.2% 중에서 무엇이 나은지 궁금합니다. 금리가 오르지 않는 한 변동금리가 이자 부담이 적습니다. 하지만 대출 기간이 긴 한 금리 변동 위험은 피할 수 없습니다. 대출을 받으려면 어떤 서류가 필요합니까? 소득이 증명되는 한 심사는 어렵지 않습니다. 다음 주에 재직증명서와 계약서를 가져오십시오. 알겠습니다. 다음 주에 부부가 함께 가져오겠습니다.
translation: Welcome. Have you come for a consultation about a housing deposit loan? Yes, we'd like to know which is better, the 3.8% fixed rate or the 3.2% variable rate. As long as rates do not rise, the variable rate has a lighter interest burden. However, as long as the loan period is long, the risk of rate changes cannot be avoided. What documents are needed to get the loan? As long as your income is verified, the review is not difficult. Please bring your employment certificate and contract next week. Understood. We'll bring them together as a couple next week.

translation: Hello, I left a black wallet on a Line 2 train this morning. I see. What does the wallet look like? It's a black leather wallet, and there is an ID card inside. I will check. As long as an ID card is inside, finding the owner is not difficult. Where can I pick it up? As long as there is no special problem, you can pick it up tomorrow at the Seoul Station lost-and-found center.

paragraph: 안녕하세요. 예약은 안 했는데 세 명 자리 있어요? 죄송합니다, 손님. 지금은 15분 정도 기다리셔야 해요. 기다릴 경우에 이름을 적어야 해요? 네, 여기에 적어 주세요. 바 자리에 앉으실 경우에 바로 안내해 드릴 수 있어요. 그럼 바 자리로 할게요. 자리가 날 경우에 옮길 수도 있나요? 네, 테이블이 비게 될 경우에 말씀해 주세요.
translation: Hello. I didn't make a reservation, but do you have a table for three? I'm sorry, sir. You'll have to wait about 15 minutes right now. In case we wait, do we need to write down our name? Yes, please write it here. If you sit at the bar counter, I can seat you right away. Then I'll take the bar seats. In case a table opens up, can we move? Yes, please tell me in case a table becomes free.

translation: Sorry, the subway stopped, so I think I'll be about 15 minutes late. It's okay. I'll order first. What do you want to drink? In case I'm even later, the ice melts. Order something hot for me. Okay, shall I order a latte? If it cools before you come, I'll ask them to reheat it. Yeah, good. In case the road is jammed, I'll text again.

In case alterations are needed, how long does it take? It usually takes three days. If you shorten the pants length, it could take one more day. Then, if I buy it today, can I receive it before Friday?

paragraph: 안녕하세요. 이번 주말에 2박으로 예약하고 싶은데요. 어쩌죠? 토요일은 방이 다 찼어요. 금요일이나 일요일만 가능해요. 일요일에 묵을 경우에 월요일 아침에 바로 출근해야 해서 힘들 것 같아요. 그러면 금요일 하루만 예약하실 경우에 다음 주 토요일은 아직 비어 있어요. 아, 그럼 다음 주말로 할게요. 취소할 경우에 언제까지 연락해야 해요? 3일 전까지만 알려 주시면 돼요.
translation: Hello. I'd like to book two nights this weekend. What to do? Saturday is fully booked. Only Friday or Sunday is available. If I stay on Sunday, I have to go straight to work Monday morning, so it'd be hard. Then if you book just Friday, next Saturday is still open. Oh, then I'll take next weekend. In case I cancel, by when do I have to contact you? Just let me know up to three days before.

paragraph: 안녕하세요, 가평 펜션이죠? 이번 주말에 2박으로 예약하고 싶어요. 죄송해요, 토요일은 방이 다 찼어요. 금요일이나 일요일은 가능해요. 그럼 금요일 하루만 잡을까요? 아니면 다른 주말이 나을까요? 금요일로 하시거든 오늘 안에 입금해 주세요. 알겠어요. 좀 더 생각해 볼게요. 다른 주말로 바꾸고 싶거든 목요일까지 전화 주세요.
translation: Hello, is this the Gapyeong pension? I'd like to book two nights this weekend. I'm sorry, Saturday is fully booked. Friday or Sunday is available. Then should I book just Friday? Or would another weekend be better? If you go with Friday, please make the deposit today. Okay. I'll think about it a bit more. If you want to switch to another weekend, call me by Thursday.

pattern.title: if... then do
pattern.explain: Say 'if this happens' and then give a request or suggestion: 시간이 있거든 = if you have time (then come).

paragraph: 민지야, 부장님이 목요일 회의를 수요일 오전 10시로 옮기셨대. 뭐? 그날 나 치과 예약 있는데. 어떡하지? 치과 끝나고 시간 되거든 온라인으로 들어와. 그래도 되나? 부장님이 화내실까 봐 걱정이야. 안 될 것 같거든 나한테 말해. 내가 회의 내용 정리해 줄게. 고마워. 일단 부장님께 물어볼게.
translation: Minji, the manager said he moved the Thursday meeting to Wednesday at 10 a.m. What? I have a dentist appointment that day. What do I do? If you have time after the dentist, join online. Is that okay? I'm worried the manager might get angry. If it seems like it won't work, tell me. I'll write up the meeting for you. Thanks. I'll ask the manager first.

If you're in a hurry, please come to the branch in three days.

pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -거든, with no change after vowels or consonants. The main clause is usually a command or suggestion.

examples.ko: 시간이 있거든 우리 집에 놀러 오세요.
examples.en: If you have time, come visit our house.
examples.rom: sigani itgeodeun uri jibe nolleo oseyo

examples.en: If there is a word you don't know, ask me.

pattern.note: Don't confuse it with sentence-ending -거든요 (giving a reason); this conditional -거든 is followed by a command or suggestion.

practice.scene: A man calls the subway lost-and-found because he left a black wallet on the Line 2 train this morning. The staff member asks what it looks like and tells him he can pick it up at Seoul Station tomorrow.

paragraph: 저기요, 지하철에 우산을 두고 내렸어요. 어떤 우산인지 말씀해 주시고, 분실물 신고서를 작성해 주세요. 파란색 장우산이에요. 비가 오기만 하면 쓰는 우산이라 꼭 찾아야 해요. 종점에서 발견되기만 하면 바로 전화드릴게요. 감사합니다. 연락처를 여기에 쓰면 되죠? 네, 맞아요.
translation: Excuse me, I left my umbrella on the subway and got off. Please tell me what kind of umbrella it is, and fill out a lost-and-found form. It's a blue long umbrella. I use it whenever it rains, so I have to find it. As soon as it's found at the last stop, I'll call you right away. Thank you. I just write my contact number here, right? Yes, that's right.

pattern.explain: Use -기만 하면 to say that one action always leads to another: 오기만 하면 = whenever (he) just comes.
pattern.attaches: Verb stem + -기만 하면, with no change after vowels or consonants. Adjectives can also be used (좋기만 하면).

practice.scene: A commuter gets off the subway and realizes he left his umbrella on the train, so he asks the station attendant for help. The attendant says to describe it and fill in a lost-and-found form, and it may be found at the last stop.

paragraph: 벌써 1시 50분이야. 5호관이 도대체 어디야? 도서관 뒤에 있을걸. 이 길로 쭉 가기만 하면 나올 거야. 아니야, 지도 앱을 보니까 공학관 옆이래. 저 언덕을 넘기만 하면 바로 보인대. 진짜? 나는 수업에 늦기만 하면 교수님이 꼭 쳐다보셔. 그러니까 뛰자! 교실에 들어가기만 하면 괜찮을 거야.
translation: It's already 1:50. Where on earth is Building 5? I think it's behind the library. If you just go straight down this road, it'll show up. No, the map app says it's next to the Engineering Building. It says that once you just cross that hill, you see it right away. Really? Whenever I'm late for class, the professor always stares at me. That's why we should run! As long as we get into the classroom, it'll be fine.

paragraph: 안녕하십니까? 다음 주 금요일 면접에 입을 양복을 사려고 합니다. 어서 오십시오. 첫 양복이시군요. 어떤 색과 디자인이 전문적으로 보입니까? 깔끔해 보이기만 하면 되는 자리라서 차콜색 양복을 추천드립니다. 수선은 얼마나 걸립니까? 사흘 걸립니다. 오늘 맡기시기만 하면 면접 전에 충분히 받으실 수 있습니다.
translation: Hello. I'd like to buy a suit to wear to my interview next Friday. Welcome. So it's your first suit. What color and cut look professional? Since it's an occasion where you only need to look neat, I recommend a charcoal suit. How long do alterations take? They take three days. As long as you leave it with us today, you can get it well before the interview.

paragraph: 회장님, 내일 아침에 안개가 낀다는데 북한산 산행은 갈 수 있을까요? 오늘 밤에 날씨를 다시 확인해 볼게요. 저는 안개가 끼기만 하면 길이 안 보일까 봐 걱정돼요. 안개가 걷히기만 하면 산행에는 문제없어요. 안개가 짙으면 어떻게 해요? 안개가 짙기만 하면 출발을 늦출 수도 있어요.
translation: Chairman, they say there'll be fog tomorrow morning. Can we still go on the Bukhansan hike? I'll check the weather again tonight. Whenever it gets foggy, I worry I won't be able to see the trail. As long as the fog lifts, there's no problem with the hike. What if the fog is thick? Whenever the fog is thick, we may start later.

paragraph: 저, 조식은 몇 시까지 하나요? 2층 식당에서 10시까지 해요. 주말에는 10시 30분까지예요. 내일 아침 일찍 나가야 한다면 도시락을 준비해 주실 수 있어요? 네, 일찍 나가신다면 오늘 저녁까지 말씀해 주세요. 감사합니다. 식당이 2층이라면 엘리베이터로 가면 되겠네요.
translation: Excuse me, until what time is breakfast served? It's served in the restaurant on the 2nd floor until 10. On weekends it's until 10:30. If I have to leave early tomorrow morning, could you prepare a boxed meal? Yes, if you're leaving early, please tell us by this evening. Thank you. If the restaurant is on the 2nd floor, I can just take the elevator.

pattern.meaning: if it is the case that
pattern.title: if it's the case that
pattern.explain: Use -다면 to say what you'll do if something turns out to be true: 비가 온다면 = if it rains.
pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -다면 (the plain form -다 plus -면). Past -았/었다면, and nouns take -(이)라면.

examples.en: If it rains tomorrow, I'll cancel the appointment.

examples.ko: 돈이 많다면 세계 여행을 하고 싶어요.
examples.en: If I had a lot of money, I would want to travel the world.
examples.rom: doni mantamyeon segye yeohaengeul hago sipeoyo

pattern.note: It treats the condition as an assumption or hypothetical, so it often sounds more tentative than -(으)면.

practice.scene: A guest asks the front desk until what time breakfast is served and where the restaurant is. The clerk explains it is on the 2nd floor until 10 a.m., but weekends end at 10:30.

paragraph: 토요일에 비가 많이 온대. 예보대로 온다면 한강 소풍은 취소해야 할 것 같아. 진짜? 나 엄청 기대했는데. 그럼 비가 온다면 영화 보러 가자. 그래, 영화관에 간다면 팝콘은 내가 살게. 좋아! 비가 안 온다면 그냥 소풍 가는 거지? 응, 날씨만 좋다면 가야지.
translation: They say it'll rain a lot on Saturday. If it comes as forecast, we'll probably have to cancel the Han River picnic. Really? I was so looking forward to it. Then if it rains, let's go to a movie. Okay, if we go to the cinema, I'll buy the popcorn. Great! If it doesn't rain, we just go on the picnic, right? Yeah, if only the weather is good, we'll go.

paragraph: 실례합니다. 경복궁에 어떻게 가면 됩니까? 걸어서 가신다면 30분 정도 걸리고, 지하철을 타신다면 10분이면 도착하십니다. 밖에 비가 오고 있습니까? 네, 지금 조금 내리고 있습니다. 계속 내린다면 지하철이 편하실 겁니다. 그렇다면 지하철로 가겠습니다. 감사합니다.
translation: Excuse me. How do I get to Gyeongbokgung Palace? If you walk, it takes about 30 minutes, and if you take the subway, you'll arrive in 10 minutes. Is it raining outside? Yes, it's raining a little now. If it keeps raining, the subway will be more convenient for you. In that case, I'll go by subway. Thank you.

paragraph: 약사님, 이 세 알은 하루에 몇 번 먹어야 해요? 하루 세 번, 식후에 드세요. 아침을 못 드신다면 간단히라도 드시고 약을 드세요. 알겠습니다. 커피를 마시고 싶은데, 마셔도 괜찮아요? 약 드시는 동안 커피를 마신다면 효과가 떨어질 수 있어요. 정말 드시고 싶다면 약 먹고 두 시간 뒤에 드세요. 그럼 오늘은 참아야겠네요. 증상이 계속된다면 다시 병원에 갈게요.
translation: Pharmacist, how many times a day should I take these three pills? Three times a day, after meals. If you can't have breakfast, eat something light and then take the medicine. Understood. I'd like to drink coffee, is it okay to drink it? If you drink coffee while taking the medicine, its effect can drop. If you really want some, have it two hours after taking the medicine. Then I'd better hold off today. If the symptoms continue, I'll go back to the hospital.

paragraph: 점심시간에 전화를 못 받아서 죄송해요. 무음으로 해 놓지 않았더라면 받았을 텐데요. 괜찮아요. 제가 미리 문자를 보냈더라면 더 좋았을 텐데요. 고마워요. 그런데 제가 도울 일이 있어요? 네, 금요일 전에 보고서 좀 봐 주실 수 있어요? 네, 오늘 퇴근 전에 볼게요.
translation: I'm sorry I couldn't take your call at lunchtime. If I hadn't left it on silent, I would have answered. It's fine. If only I had sent a text beforehand, it would have been better. Thanks. By the way, is there something I can help with? Yes, could you look over my report before Friday? Sure, I'll look at it before I leave work today.

pattern.title: if only I had
pattern.explain: Use -았/었더라면 to wish the past had gone differently, saying what would have happened: 공부했더라면 = if only I had studied.
pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -았더라면 after ㅏ/ㅗ (갔더라면), -었더라면 after other vowels (먹었더라면), and 하다 becomes 했더라면.

examples.en: If I had studied hard then, I would have passed.
If we had left early, we wouldn't have been late.

pattern.note: It describes an unreal past condition and the main clause usually expresses regret or a different outcome, such as -았/었을 텐데.

practice.scene: A coworker-turned-friend texts B to say sorry for missing a call during lunch because the phone was on silent. B says it's fine and asks whether A can look over a report before Friday.

paragraph: 토요일에 비가 많이 온대. 한강 소풍 취소될지도 몰라. 정말? 날씨를 미리 알았더라면 다른 날로 잡았을 텐데. 그러게. 일기예보를 좀 더 일찍 봤더라면 좋았을 텐데. 아쉽다. 비 오면 영화나 보러 갈까? 좋아, 그러자.
translation: They say it'll rain a lot on Saturday. The Han River picnic might get canceled. Really? If only I had known the weather in advance, I would have picked another day. I know. It would have been good if I had checked the forecast a bit earlier. What a pity. If it rains, shall we go see a movie or something? Sounds good, let's do that.

pattern.attaches: Verb or adjective stem + -았더라면 after ㅏ/ㅗ (갔더라면), -었더라면 after other vowels (먹었더라면), and 하다 becomes 했더라면.

examples.en: If I had studied hard then, I would have passed.
If we had left early, we wouldn't have been late.

pattern.note: It describes an unreal past condition and the main clause usually expresses regret or a different outcome, such as -았/었을 텐데.

practice.scene: A tells younger sister B that the Han River picnic might be canceled because the forecast says heavy rain on Saturday. B is disappointed and suggests going to a movie if it rains.

paragraph: 팀장님, 안녕하십니까? 2호선이 신호 문제로 멈춰서 출근이 늦어질 것 같습니다. 그렇습니까? 몇 시쯤 도착하실 수 있습니까? 9시 30분쯤 도착할 것 같습니다. 10분만 일찍 나왔더라면 제시간에 도착했을 텐데 죄송합니다. 괜찮습니다. 9시 30분 회의에는 전화로 참석할 수 있습니까? 네, 가능합니다. 회의 자료를 어제 보내 드렸더라면 좋았을 텐데, 지금 바로 메일로 보내겠습니다.
translation: Team leader, hello. Line 2 has stopped because of a signal problem, so I think I'll be late to work. Is that so? About what time can you arrive? I think I'll arrive around 9:30. If only I had left 10 minutes earlier, I would have arrived on time. I'm sorry. It's all right. Can you join the 9:30 meeting by phone? Yes, I can. It would have been good if I had sent the meeting materials yesterday; I'll email them right now.

paragraph: 여보세요? 30분이면 된다고 했는데 벌써 한 시간이나 지났어요. 정말 죄송해요, 고객님. 성함이 어떻게 되세요? 김민수예요. 처음부터 오래 걸린다고 말씀해 주셨더라면 다른 곳에 시켰을 거예요. 확인했어요. 저희가 미리 안내해 드렸더라면 좋았을 텐데 죄송해요. 기사님이 2분 뒤에 도착해요. 알겠어요. 기다릴게요.
translation: Hello? You said it would take 30 minutes, but a whole hour has already passed. I'm really sorry, customer. What is your name? It's Kim Minsu. If only you had told me from the start that it would take long, I would have ordered from somewhere else. I've checked. It would have been good if we had informed you beforehand; I'm sorry. The driver will arrive in two minutes. Okay. I'll wait.
